title: Backtest decision D87 against real records, read-only
summary: Add a read-only Rust backtest: typed headers for D87 and D88 only, a parser for the supersession phrases in docs/decisions.md, and Athena code that reads records/ for D87-era landings and interventions. It runs one exact-match signal (2 jobs, from stored fields) and writes one introspection record for the earliest matching event naming D87. The result is reported as pass or fail under review section 5, and a fail is written up as a finding.

defaults_applied.how: The parser, record reader, signal and tests are Rust.
Unit tests for the parser and signal; cargo test and clippy must pass.
The findings report cites record ids and labels any estimate.
One build limited to D87 and D88 and a single signal.
A fail is reported with its cause, not patched to pass.
Record ids and job ids only; no personal data or email addresses in output.
The report and docs are written for an outside reader.
Use existing parsing crates already in the workspace (such as toml and serde), and no new dependency unless needed.

assumptions: The backtest is Rust code with tests, placed in athena-data (typed header, supersession parser, record reading) and exposed through a read-only command in athena-cli or xtask. I did not read those crates, so the exact home is a guess.
The typed headers for D87 and D88 live in a new file under docs/ (for example docs/decisions-typed.toml), not inside docs/decisions.md, because Athena never edits a decision.
D87's enforcement is written as brief/design, not code-check, as review finding F4 says.
records/ is absent from the reader's copy. Record ids and counts are unknown until the code runs, so the result is not predictable. A fail is a legitimate outcome.

The introspection record is a new record file written once for the earliest matching event. The review says it is written by a language model and reviewed by a person, but the request says no Jev. So the code assembles the record deterministically from stored fields, with decisions_matched = [D87], and earlier_cases is checked by code. Any model-written prose is marked as such and left for human review.
The supersession parse is case-insensitive. It must return D46->D79 (lines 1020 and 1752) and D87->D88 (lines 1901 and 1922) plus the Amends entries, with no entry lacking a target id.
The findings report is a short docs/design/ file recording the pass/fail result, the cited ids and the reason.

acceptance_criteria.text: A typed header exists for D87 and D88 only, with kind, scope, status, enforcement, assumptions and signals. D87's enforcement is not code-check. D87 is marked amended_by D88.

Running cargo test passes. It includes a test that the supersession parser over docs/decisions.md returns the D46->D79 and D87->D88 hits plus the Amends entries, matched case-insensitively, with no entry lacking a target id.
cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check are clean.

Running the backtest command with cargo run reads records/ in code, with no agent or model call and no gateway client. It prints the D87-era landing and intervention record ids found, and the verdict from the single exact-match signal.

The signal passes only if it marks D87 under-review citing at least 2 distinct job ids and their intervention ids, all existing in records/. Run over the same records it marks no other typed decision, D88 included. Otherwise the result is reported as a fail with the reason, and the signal is not tuned to pass.

One introspection record is written for the earliest matching event naming D87. It has a decisions_matched field containing D87, and every earlier_cases id exists and is in the same class. If the signal found nothing, no record is written and the report says so.
A findings report states the actual result (pass or fail), the record ids cited, and the reason for a fail. It labels unmeasured numbers as estimates.
The change makes no edit to docs/decisions.md, defaults.toml, briefs, or any Jev or gateway code.

out_of_scope: Any Jev or gateway call, or a client for one
Any change to briefs, readers, producers or verifiers, or to budgets
Typed headers for any decision other than D87 and D88
The host-error record (review F3) and the other design fixes in review section 6
Writing introspection records for events other than the earliest D87 match
departures: Higher than the reference. The work is new code in a few crates plus real-record reading whose shape is unseen, and the pass/fail verification needs records/ content.
